methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 18.4x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Ranovus is a Series D+ semiconductor company that has raised $236M in total funding, including a $36M strategic investment fund grant in August 2025. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 12 same-sector peers in Chips & Semiconductors, comprising 3 public companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private firms including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, SambaNova Systems, Etched, and Ayar Labs.

Two standard valuation approaches were evaluated. Peer-median multiples proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow peer data: while 12 same-sector peers exist, zero companies met the narrower criteria of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparability, falling short of the minimum three datapoints needed for reliable triangulation. Public-comp anchoring using the Semiconductors sector P/S median of 18.4x across the three public tickers was also not applicable, as Ranovus's revenue is not disclosed—a common constraint for private company valuation.

The absence of sufficient quantitative anchors from either method means this analysis cannot support a specific valuation range on the data provided. Key uncertainties include Ranovus's undisclosed revenue, margin profile, and the heterogeneity of the private peer set across different technical and market segments within semiconductors. A valuation conclusion would require either disclosure of revenue and profitability metrics, or identification of additional same-stage or similar-tier private comparables with disclosed terms.
